cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 takes up T3's ask-the-livers advice and narrows it: ask many, privately, the quiet ones.
cells.limitation: T5 answers 'you cannot trial-run a marriage' as the Skeptic's objection; T3 never made it.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T5 introduces milestones as bundles of pieces; T6 and section E build on testing one piece.
cells.limitation: T10 mostly recaps positions and adds little beyond T9.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Comparison versus desire (T1-T2) and freedom versus belonging (T8) are both examined.
cells.limitation: Family or parental expectations and age-related timing never raised by any mind.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T4 grants surrogates beat introspection; T6 accepts bundling but adds novelty bias to trials.
cells.limitation: T10's shift is framed against a claim (feeling is false) nobody held, blurring real integration.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates the feeling of lag from the question of wanting; disputed source named.
cells.limitation: T10 ends on a recap rather than sharpening the exclusion-versus-longing test further.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T8 states the Anthropologist's exclusion reading fairly before offering the longing alternative.
cells.limitation: T10 recasts T1 as 'the feeling is false'; T1 only said it sounded like comparison.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption that friends are neutral witnesses and why their reports are filtered.
cells.limitation: T6's novelty-bias objection to trials is never answered by the Experimenter in T8.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 invidious comparison and T3 surrogate advice fit Veblen and Gilbert respectively.
cells.limitation: T9 'Many people are only behind for a stretch' is an unsupported generalisation.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T7 frames exclusion as a bet and flags 'my extension, not his claim'.
cells.limitation: T9 states the feeling usually fades as fact rather than hypothesis.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 concedes surrogates beat introspection, then narrows rather than retreats.
cells.limitation: T10's 'we have shifted' names no specific argument that caused the revision.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A names the ambiguity: lag could be missing out, closeness, money, or being measured.
cells.limitation: Whether 'behind' is measured against age or a personal timeline is never probed.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T2 turns the user's 'not sure' into a distinction from 'do not want', reshaping the argument.
cells.limitation: T5 assumes the user rents and is single; neither is stated.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 refuses to rank freedom and belonging: 'That ranking belongs to you'.
cells.limitation: T1 leans on the user's doubt as the more trustworthy signal, a speaker preference.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T9 makes waiting conditional on whether a real clock is running; E branches on money.
cells.limitation: T5 invents renting and singleness to design cheap tests.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T6 asks envy, drifting, or money and E states what each answer implies.
cells.limitation: Relationship status and age, both consequential for E's trials, are neither asked nor branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T7 exclusion versus T8 longing in a comparison costume, offered with T6's answerable question.
cells.limitation: T7's bet leans toward exclusion before the user has answered.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2: not sure is not the same as not wanting; T3 exposes both as forecasts.
cells.limitation: The assumption that friends' timeline is the right yardstick is touched only indirectly in T4.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8 names freedom and belonging in conflict and says trials show which hurts to lose.
cells.limitation: T8 adds 'Maybe security as well' without developing what security means here.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T6 names fear of drifting from friends; T4 names social pressure without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Family or cultural expectation, a common source of feeling behind, is absent throughout.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D closes with a question the user can answer: what is left when the feeling goes.
cells.limitation: T7's bet offers the user a ready answer before the question is posed.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Waiting (T9), small trials (T5), tending friendships (T7), practical planning (E) are all present.
cells.limitation: Options are scattered across turns; only section E gathers them.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T6 gives the cost of trials: novelty or doing it alone can make them feel flat.
cells.limitation: Costs of reworking friendships or of ignoring the feeling are never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: E: eases picturing an unconventional life but returns picturing years alone favours a small trial.
cells.limitation: E's 'a few weeks' observation window is not derived from the user's facts.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A says the source of the lag is the unknown that matters most.
cells.limitation: Whether any real clock is running is raised in T9 but left unranked against other unknowns.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: E: talk privately with people who took these steps and note gains and losses.
cells.limitation: E's 'a few people' and 'a few weeks' are loose rather than tied to the situation.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 'real longing wearing a comparison costume' is plain and precise.
cells.limitation: T4 'surrogates' is unexplained shorthand for other people's reports.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T7 'I will bet on the second' points cleanly to T6's list.
cells.limitation: T9 'concede a point to the Anthropologist' never says which point or turn.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within range; each turn carries one move.
cells.limitation: Section E is one long paragraph with four branches, heavy to scan.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: T10 states an explicit position change; the three lenses stay distinct.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one measured register and similar turn lengths.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely repeat; T5's bundle list is compact.
cells.limitation: T10 recaps the Experimenter's and Skeptic's positions already stated.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T7: friends moving into a shared script means fewer shared evenings.
cells.limitation: Tension stays mild; no mind presses what happens if the user waits and is wrong.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T4 grants surrogates after T3's argument; T9 unexpectedly argues for doing nothing.
cells.limitation: T10's reversal names no earlier argument as its cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T3 Skeptic: 'You both sound sure of yourselves, which worries me.'
cells.limitation: Veblen's sardonic edge appears once (T4); voices otherwise similar in tone.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T4: nobody announces the mortgage was a mistake at the housewarming.
cells.limitation: T9 and T10 carry no comparable image or sharp line.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T6's three-way question builds toward T7's bet and T8's refusal.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths and intensity are even throughout; little change of rhythm.

strengths: Section A and T6 turn the key unknown (envy, drifting, money) into a question whose answers section E branches on.
T5's bundle distinction is new mid-debate and reused in T6 and section E's small-trial branch.
T7-T8 offer exclusion and real longing as competing motives, with T8 leaving the ranking to the user.
weaknesses: T10's shift names no causing argument and misstates T1 as calling the feeling false.
T5 invents context (renting, being single) to design tests; relationship status is never asked.
T9 states that the feeling usually fades as fact, without support.

symptoms.observed: Position change attributed to no specific earlier argument; recasts own prior claim.
symptoms.evidence: Then we have shifted. I no longer say the feeling is false

symptoms.observed: Proposes tests assuming the user rents and is single; neither stated.
symptoms.evidence: renting longer-term somewhere, hosting dinners, a serious relationship

symptoms.observed: Generalisation about the feeling fading offered without basis or hedge.
symptoms.evidence: Many people are only behind for a stretch, and the feeling fades

symptoms.observed: Novelty-bias objection to trials goes unanswered by the Experimenter.
Concession names a mind but not which point is conceded.
symptoms.evidence: I will concede a point to the Anthropologist

findings.description: Claim that being behind usually passes is stated as general fact without support.
Assumes the user rents and lacks a serious relationship; the situation states neither.
Quoted term invidious comparison is consistent with Veblen's usage; not checkable here.

rubric_fit_notes: The situation gives very little personal detail, so C3.2 and C3.4 rest mostly on how the debate handled absent facts; the decision is implicit (what to do about the feeling), which the debate treated reasonably.
raw.question_type_note: Read as a decision about how to respond to the feeling of being behind, with self-reflection weighting criterion 4 heavily.
